high.title: Additional 2 Units Apply for Gold Bar Production and Gold Import Licenses, SBV Under Review
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) reports that 11 entities, including enterprises and credit institutions, have now submitted applications for gold bar production and raw gold import licenses - an increase of 2 applications since the beginning of the year. SBV's Foreign Exchange Management Department Director Dao Xuan Tuan confirmed the central bank is coordinating with relevant ministries and agencies to review licensing for qualified units. The licensing process involves close cooperation between multiple departments with regular consultations to ensure transparency and regulatory compliance. After gold bar production licenses are granted, SBV will consider import permits for entities meeting all requirements. This development is significant for Vietnam's gold market regulation and could impact domestic gold supply dynamics, potentially affecting the VND gold price differential with international markets.

high.title: VN-Index Reclaims 1,800 Points, Why Are Many Investors Still Not Happy?
high.summary: VN-Index surged 1.41% (+25 points) to close at 1,800.65 points on April 15, driven primarily by Vingroup-related stocks. VIC hit ceiling price (+6.9%), contributing 18.75 points to the index, while VHM added 7.04 points with a 6.3% gain. Trading volume on HoSE reached 910.7 million shares worth VND 24,431 billion. VN30 rose to 1,961.60 points with VND 12,339 billion in trading value. Despite the strong headline performance, market breadth remained mixed with profit-taking pressure emerging in many sectors during the afternoon session. The heavy reliance on Vingroup stocks for the index recovery raises concerns about market concentration risk and sustainability of the rally, which may explain investor caution despite the psychological 1,800 breakthrough.

medium.title: April 14: Gold Bar and Smooth Ring Gold Prices Rise Across the Board
medium.summary: Gold prices increased significantly on April 14, with SJC gold bars rising to VND 170.5-173.0 million per tael at major dealers. Gold rings were priced at VND 169.7-172.7 million per tael. The price increases occurred in multiple waves throughout the day, starting from VND 168.5-171.5 million per tael in the morning. This reflects continued volatility in Vietnam's domestic gold market amid regulatory changes and international price movements.

medium.title: MASVN: There is Basis to Assume VN-Index Has Formed a Bottom
medium.summary: Mirae Asset Vietnam draws parallels between current market conditions and April 2025, when markets bottomed after Trump announced negotiation delays. The firm notes that markets typically bottom when uncertainty peaks and signals shift from "escalation" to "negotiation." With US 10-year Treasury yields previously exceeding 4.3% before Trump's March 23 announcement postponing Iran strikes, similar patterns suggest Vietnamese equities may have found a floor. This analysis supports a more constructive outlook for VND-denominated assets.

medium.title: Expert: VN-Index's 2,000-Point Target Still Has Basis for Expectation
medium.summary: VCBF's Nguyen Duy Anh identifies three key market drivers: interest rates, inflation, and capital flows. Vietnam's interest rates rose from 5-6% to 7-8% since late 2025, making deposits more attractive versus equities. This stems from high credit growth outpacing deposit mobilization, forcing banks to raise rates. However, more cautious regulatory guidance may help moderate rate pressures, supporting the 2,000-point target for VN-Index.

medium.title: Afternoon April 15: SJC Gold and Ring Gold Prices Both Turn Down
medium.summary: Gold prices reversed course on April 15 afternoon, falling VND 1.5-2.5 million per tael from morning levels. SJC gold bars traded at VND 170.5-174.0 million per tael at major dealers, while buy-sell spreads widened from VND 2.5 million to VND 3.5 million per tael. International gold prices also declined toward $4,800/ounce, pressuring domestic prices and reflecting continued volatility in both global and Vietnamese gold markets.
